designPrinciple: A beginner first receives a bounded explanation or demonstration, predicts and traces behavior, then writes, breaks, repairs, tests, explains, and proves a progressively less scaffolded program.
targetLearner: A tertiary fresher or independent beginner with basic computer literacy and no assumed programming experience
technologySequence: values, decisions, and narrow error handling
learningRhythm: required Build in sessions of at most two hours

resourceRoleStrategy.learn: A short first explanation or visual demonstration.
resourceRoleStrategy.practice: An observable prediction, trace, run, or comparison.
resourceRoleStrategy.reference: A precise bounded lookup beside immediate work, never an unscoped documentation dump.

progressionPolicy: Weeks 4–6 combine earlier syntax in distinct small programs.
Week 8 integrates proven competencies into one larger independently inspectable project.
workloadPrinciples: Eight instructional Weeks at six hours each.
Setup is separate and skippable only through explicit verification.
No Build session exceeds two hours.
Most time is reserved for coding, debugging, tests, evidence, and explanation rather than passive consumption.
assessmentPolicy: Each Week has ten independently authored, source-mapped questions; 7/10 passes; attempts are unlimited; option order reshuffles per attempt; program competence is judged through Build and Proof, not quiz score alone.

projectArchitecture.title: Python Practice Portfolio
projectArchitecture.outcome: Produce seven progressively stronger programs demonstrating execution, values, decisions, collections, functions, persistence, objects, modules, tests, and debugging.

projectArchitecture.title: TaskTrail CLI
projectArchitecture.outcome: Deliver and publish a tested, persistent campus-task command-line program with a reproducible README and human-reviewable evidence.
